reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3, E4) directly supports the fabrication of nanostructured, textured refractory HEA films/pillars and the resulting ultrahigh strength, improved ductility, and thermal stability, but only for the NbMoTaW alloy. The hypothesis assumes, without specific evidence, that this strategy will work identically for TiVNbTa, which is a different alloy system. E1 is about nanoscale chemical fluctuations in CCAs and does not directly support the key premises.
premises: Nanoscale grain structure and strong texture can be fabricated in refractory HEA thin films or pillars
Such nanostructured HEA pillars exhibit ultrahigh yield strength (~10 GPa) and improved ductility (>30% compressive strain)
Such nanostructured HEA films show enhanced stability under high-temperature, long-duration conditions (1100°C for 3 days)
These property improvements are demonstrated in the refractory HEA NbMoTaW
The same fabrication strategy and resulting property enhancements will transfer to the TiVNbTa alloy system
